newsitem.title: FRANCE: Cold dogs French holiday-makers on trip home.
newsitem.headline: Cold dogs French holiday-makers on trip home.

text.p: Cold weather lengthened journeys home for thousands of French holiday-makers on Sunday, closing several motorways in the southwest, trimming train services and virtually sealing off a few Pyrenees ski resorts.
The national road traffic centre urged those facing the difficult trip home from the Bordeaux region in the southwest or from central France, both badly hit by snow and ice, to extend their holidays.
Several hundred travellers spent Saturday night in schools and municipal halls after the A20 motorway in the Limousin region was closed. Traffic restarted at dawn but only on one lane.

Other drivers were stranded in the Charente and Charente-Maritime regions, and in the Gers department schoolchildren were given an extra day's holiday and some 7,000 households had no electricity supply.

The Gers regional authority urged the prefect (central government representative) to declare a "national catastrophe" in parts of the region to win help with resources and manpower to clear roads and restore power supplies.
Further south in the Pyrenees, three ski resorts were completely sealed off by heavy snowfalls. Three other resorts organised convoys of some 100 vehicles each to allow some skiers to leave.
In the Rhone Valley near Lyon in central France, fresh snowfalls on Sunday seriously disrupted traffic on the A7 Autoroute du Soleil (Sun Motorway) towards Orange.
Traffic was also hit further east near Grenoble at the foot of the French Alps. A 17-year-old skier died in an avalanche near the village of Termignon in the Savoie region, local officials said.
On Sunday, two rescuers from the Val Frejus ski resort nearby were caught offguard by a snowslide and taken to hospital for observation.
Rail travel was also disrupted, with six high-speed TGV electric trains laid on from Bordeaux in the southwest to Paris after technicians managed to clear the track.

TGVs had for two days been replaced on the Bordeaux-Paris track by slower diesel-powered locomotives, but SNCF railway officials said they had managed to ferry some 17,000 passengers on Sunday, around the norm, although with delays.
Traffic between Marseille and Paris was down to one in two scheduled TGV trains after ice built up to 10 cm (four inches) in diameter on power lines, halting the electric trains.

Meteo France weather forecasters said the cold was likely to worsen on Monday and would last several days. The institute said temperatures would slip below minus 10 Celsius (14 Fahrenheit) in northern France early in the week.
